subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class named session snapshots now, and if so should the first supported scope be arbitrary save/list/load, archive restore, checkpoint branch/restore, or prompt-cache-aware fork?
rationale: The source shows multiple adjacent primitives but no single product contract for named snapshots, and choosing destructive restore, branch, retention, and archive-import semantics is a maintainer product/API decision rather than a narrow code repair.

options.title: Design core snapshot API first
options.body: Create a maintainer-owned design that unifies named checkpoints, restore/branch behavior, archive import, privacy rules, and protocol/command surfaces before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to resume/archive restore
options.body: Let a focused `/resume` or archive-restore path land first while keeping named checkpoints and deterministic snapshot diff tracked separately.

options.title: Defer named snapshots
options.body: Keep compaction checkpoints, export commands, and `sessions_spawn` fork as separate primitives and close or split broader snapshot work later.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot API first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-owned design that unifies named checkpoints, restore/branch behavior, archive import, privacy rules, and protocol/command surfaces before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review comment and recent session lifecycle work make this the best available owner for deciding the product/API scope.
